name: The desk says, before the click, whether a screen is already recorded under the pins a run would resolve now
notes: Verified goal-desk-iter-36 by browser-qa-agent (2026-07-31). THREE states captured with screenshots: (1) match -- a fixture-scoped rig (scoped backend :8391 over a scratch universe/bars/screen store, seeded from the committed universe+AAPL-daily fixtures used by test_desk_screen_pins.py's own real_ctx, plus a scoped frontend on :3391 via NEXT_DIST_DIR=.next-iter36-qa so the ambient .next was never touched) recorded a real screen for 2026-06-22 via run_screen_and_record, then reloaded /desk: the Provenance panel's resolved-pins block named the exact recorded snapshot ('A screen is recorded under these exact pins — screen-2026-06-22-09cf660a4125, recorded 2026-07-31T13:22:41.106918Z.') -- reports/qa/goal-desk-iter-36-evidence/J-21-match.png. (2) differ -- the AMBIENT :3301/:8301 rig, read-only, no click: the Provenance panel and the Run-Screen-control line both stated no screen is recorded under the pins that resolve right now (bar_store_signature 2ce14e8f252966f7 vs the displayed screen's own ae2c740d1a70c9c7), each naming 'a run would walk 101 members' -- reports/qa/goal-desk-iter-36-evidence/J-21-differ.png. (3) empty -- the SAME fixture-scoped rig BEFORE any registration in that session: 'No universe snapshot is registered — whether a run today would reuse a recorded screen cannot be named.' rendered beside the Run Screen button in the honest empty-state panel -- reports/qa/goal-desk-iter-36-evidence/J-21-empty.png. All three captures were at 1440x900 with scrollWidth==clientWidth (no horizontal scroll), ranked/empty-state table rendering exactly as J-16/J-04 shipped it. The scoped rig was torn down after use (both processes killed, apps/frontend/.next-iter36-qa removed, next-env.d.ts/tsconfig.json restored to their pre-rig md5sums) -- the ambient .next was never rebuilt (iter-26 lesson).

This script targets the AMBIENT rig only (relative goto urls) and DELIBERATELY asserts stable, state-independent structure rather than the match/differ narrative text, per the J-18/J-19/J-20 hardening precedent ('journey-scripts/*.json must assert stable substrings, never a specific run's exact ids/counts'): whichever of the two states the ambient store happens to be in on a future replay (a Run Screen click could flip today's own pins to 'match' at any time), the pin-disclosure BLOCKS themselves are structurally always present once any screen exists (desk-provenance-pins) and beside the Run Screen control in every state including the pre-registration empty one (one of desk-run-screen-pins-match/-differ/-empty always renders, never all absent) -- so this script cannot be invalidated by a future ambient Run Screen click the way a literal 'no screen is recorded...walk 101 members' pin would be.

Step 2's testid existence check (desk-provenance-pins) plus its step-level text assertion ('Pins resolved right now for this screen date') is the fixed LABEL every DeskProvenance render shows regardless of match/differ sub-state -- never the flip-floppy sentence below it.

Step 3 checks for ANY of the three run-screen-pins-note testids via a comma-separated CSS selector (Playwright OR-selector) -- true in the empty state (no universe), the match state, and the differ state alike, so it never needs updating when the ambient store's own reuse-vs-walk answer changes.
Step 4 is a post-match liveness check (the iter-4/iter-5 lesson): a further /desk navigation after the key assertions, proving the page is still alive and rendering correctly.

UPDATED (desk section collapse) by developer: six /desk sections now render COLLAPSED -- Screen Runs, Screen Comparison, Provenance, Index Reconciliation, Top-up Runs and Playbook Evidence are on the page and named, but closed by default, and each one's own GET is deferred until its first expand. Their headings stay VISIBLE while closed, so a step that pins a section TITLE still resolves untouched; only a step reading a section's CONTENTS needs the expand click inserted before it, because the replay runner resolves every target with state="visible". This is a deliberate product-shape change, not a regression.

expect.text: Pins resolved right now for this screen date
